query: Prior studies of Al-containing Cr–Co–Fe–Ni alloys showed that composition and thermal history can substantially alter constituent phases and transformation behavior, but they did not establish a predictive explanation of phase stability across the relevant thermal regime or adequately connect it to composition-dependent thermodynamic instability. Given the competing thermodynamic and kinetic factors in multicomponent alloys, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains what governs phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially in a high-temperature BCC state and why? State a controlled comparison and baseline, predicted observations, boundary conditions, prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In the Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 high-temperature single-phase BCC (A2) alloy, phase stability on cooling is governed by the onset of Ni–Al chemical short-range ordering. Below a characteristic ordering temperature (T_ord ≃ 950 ± 50 °C) the enthalpic gain from forming Ni–Al-rich B2-type order outweighs the TΔS_conf term that stabilises the random BCC solid solution at higher temperature. Emergence of B2 clusters first lowers the free energy; their growth partitions Ni and Al into the ordered domains and enriches the residual matrix in Cr (and Fe), which subsequently promotes σ or Cr-rich A2 precipitation. Therefore, Ni–Al ordering is the mechanistic trigger that controls whether the initially stable high-T BCC phase persists or decomposes on cooling/aging.
generation.material_initial_state: Homogenised Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 alloy, solution-treated at 1200 °C for 2 h to produce a single-phase disordered BCC (A2) solid solution, then water-quenched to preserve that state.
generation.intervention: Isothermal aging for 1–100 h at 700, 800, 900 and 1000 °C under inert atmosphere, compared with (i) a rapid water-quench (no aging) and (ii) an Al-lean reference alloy Cr39Co18Fe20Ni18Al5 aged identically.
generation.conditions: High-vacuum or Ar back-filled sealed quartz tubes; temperature control ±10 °C; quench rate >100 °C s⁻¹ after aging.
generation.structural_mediator: Development of Ni–Al–rich B2 short-range order (and subsequent coherent B2 precipitates) within the parent BCC matrix.
generation.mechanism: ΔG_mix = ΔH_mix – TΔS_conf controls stability. At high T, the large positive configurational entropy (ΔS_conf) keeps the random A2 solid solution stable. As temperature drops, the negative ordering enthalpy (ΔH_order) for Ni–Al pairs drives formation of B2-type SRO. Once B2 embryos nucleate, they sequester Ni and Al, enriching the surrounding matrix in Cr/Fe/Co; this chemical partitioning destabilises the matrix and drives secondary σ or Cr-rich A2 precipitation. Thus, Ni–Al ordering is the primary trigger, and the transformation sequence BCC(A2) → B2 + (σ or Cr-rich A2) is entropy–enthalpy governed.
generation.predicted_outcome: 1. Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 aged at 700–900 °C will show B2 superlattice reflections in X-ray/neutron/SAD patterns within ≤1 h, with ~5–15 vol % B2 after 100 h and concomitant hardness increase of ≈300 MPa over the as-quenched state. 2. σ phase appears only after measurable B2 has formed and will be Cr-rich (>55 at % Cr). 3. Aging at ≥1000 °C preserves a single-phase A2 structure with only diffuse B2-type SRO scattering and <50 MPa hardness change. 4. The Al-lean reference alloy will remain single-phase A2 and show no B2/σ even after 100 h at 800 °C, confirming the role of Ni–Al ordering.
generation.baseline: As-quenched Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7: single-phase disordered BCC (A2); hardness ≈HV 250; no sharp B2 superlattice peaks, only weak diffuse scattering indicative of incipient Ni–Al SRO.
generation.boundary: Hypothesis expected to hold for compositions with 6–9 at % Al and Ni/Al ratio ≈2–3 and for temperatures below ~1000 °C but above the martensitic range; fails if Al <5 at % or if cooling rates are fast enough to eliminate measurable diffusion (t <10 min at T <700 °C).
generation.uncertainty: Exact value of T_ord and B2 volume fraction depend on grain size, prior defects and minor impurities; the sequence σ vs. Cr-rich A2 may vary with these factors. Partitioning behaviour of Co is less certain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two alloys: (a) Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 and (b) Cr39Co18Fe20Ni18Al5. Homogenise at 1200 °C/2 h, water-quench. Age both at 800 °C for 1 h, 10 h, 100 h and at 1000 °C for 10 h. After each treatment, characterise phases by synchrotron XRD and TEM/SAD, measure hardness (microhardness or nanoindentation), and perform APT or STEM-EDS for elemental partitioning.
measurements: Presence and intensity of B2 superlattice peaks (XRD/TEM)
Volume fraction of B2 and σ phases (Rietveld analysis)
Elemental partitioning profiles around precipitates (APT or STEM-EDS)
Vickers or nano-indentation hardness change relative to baseline
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if ANY of the following occur: (1) Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 aged at 800 °C shows σ or Cr-rich A2 precipitation WITHOUT prior or concurrent B2 ordering; (2) B2 or σ phases appear in the Al-lean reference alloy under identical conditions; (3) Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 remains single-phase A2 with no B2 superlattice peaks after 100 h aging at 800 °C.
